title: fix(plugin-auth): SCIM adopts an account SSO JIT created when the three ruled conditions hold, and its 409 no longer names the vendor
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg8egaeLeSDHBS4fiLJJ1EYo)_
domain:devx#2 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CaA8pcS7BEcMt15WeW

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：客户先开 SSO、后开 SCIM 时，Entra ID / Okta 给「开 SCIM 前已用 SSO 登录过的员工」建号，不再一律 409；当账号满足裁决的三条件时，直接把这个已有账号接到该 SCIM 连接上（返回 201，之后的停用、组推送都能落到这个人身上）。其余情形照旧 409，且 409 文案不再出现第三方库的名字。
- 为什么改：裁决 A（6810486663）。不改的话，凡是先用 SSO 登录过的员工都同步失败，离职停用漏掉这些人。
- 风险与回滚：只走库自带的 `identity.resolveUser` 挂点，不改库、不重写协议。接管须同时满足：账号是 `idp_provisioned` 且没有本地密码；没被任何 SCIM 目录持有过（含已被别的目录删除的离职账号）；链接到本组织的 SSO 提供方；邮箱域名正是该提供方已验证的域名（要开 `OS_SSO_DOMAIN_VERIFICATION` 并验证域名才会生效）。绝不按裸邮箱匹配。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`scim-sso-adoption.ts` 的 `judgeScimSsoAdoption`（判定顺序与每条拒绝理由）；`auth-manager-plugin-list.ts` 的 `resolveUser` 接线；`scim-conflict-detail.ts` 与 `auth-manager-request-routing.ts` 的 409 文案翻译。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/scim-sso-adoption.test.ts`，预期 17/17 通过（真 `@better-auth/scim` + sqlite：两条接管、十一种拒绝、一条照常新建、三条文案）。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

Fixes #32148

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — `git grep -n -i scim -- 'skills/**'` has no hit; the hand-written SCIM text in `content/docs/**` (`permissions/authentication.mdx` "SCIM Connection Credentials", `permissions/sso.mdx` group mappings) covers the credential door and group mappings, and no page states what a SCIM create does with an existing account.

**On `Clause-②: no`** (copied from the claim), said plainly as the order asks: no published contract accept set widens. The SCIM request schema, every validation refusal and every spec surface are unchanged. What widens is a runtime identity boundary: under the conditions below, a `POST /Users` that answered `409` now links an existing account and answers `201`. That is the security / identity class (`execution-duties.md`: a runtime permission or security behaviour change is not Clause ②), which is why the contract review runs at the ceiling tier and security#2 was told at claim.

## What changes

### The seam (Step 0, measured on `@better-auth/scim` 1.7.12)

The library has a host callback for exactly this: `identity.resolveUser(input, { database })` returns `{ action: 'create' }` or `{ action: 'link', userId, profile }` (`dist/index.d.mts:231-266`, with the library's own rule "Returning `link` must not be based on an unverified email match"). `POST /Users` asks it before its transaction (`dist/index.mjs:6984`), and on `link` writes the SCIM resource against that account inside its transaction (`7011-7018`). The platform passed only `identity.reconcileUser`; `resolveUser` now sits beside it. No library change, no protocol re-implementation.

The door is the create. The lookup (`GET /Users?filter=userName eq "…"`, `dist/index.mjs:7120`, reading only the connection's own `scimUser` rows at `7161-7166`) has no host hook and needs none: Entra ID and Okta look up (0), then create; the create links and answers `201` with a new SCIM id, and every later lookup finds it.

### `scim-sso-adoption.ts` (new)

`judgeScimSsoAdoption` reads, as the system, and answers adopt or one refusal reason. `link` only when every part holds, in this order:

| Step | Holds when | Refusal reason |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `sys_user.source = 'idp_provisioned'` (ruled condition 1) | `not_directory_managed` |
| 1 | no `credential` `sys_account` (ADR-0135 D4's own reading of directory-managed, as `markDirectoryProvisionedUsers`) | `holds_local_password` |
| 2 | no `sys_scim_subject` row for the account | `held_by_scim` |
| 3 | one of its `sys_account` rows names a `sys_sso_provider` (ruled condition 2) | `no_sso_link` |
| 3 | that provider's `organization_id` equals the organization of the credential that authenticated the request (`sys_scim_connection_credential.organization_id`, read off the request's SCIM scope); both unset = one environment-wide boundary, one unset = refuse | `no_provider_of_organization` |
| 4 | that provider reads `domain_verified` (ruled condition 3, ADR-0135 D6) | `domain_not_verified` |
| 4 | the account's email domain is exactly one of the provider's `domain` entries (comma list, case-folded, no subdomain match) | `email_domain_not_verified` |

Any refusal resolves to `create`, which collides on the email and answers `409` as before. No account with the address: `create`, a new user, as before. `createScimSsoAdoptionResolver` also answers `create` when the request carries no SCIM scope or a scope naming another connection: the organization cannot be read, so nothing is adopted. A link uses `profile: 'manage'`, so the directory manages the adopted profile like one it created, and the vendor's in-transaction profile claim refuses if another SCIM source took the profile between the read and the write.

**How the predicate stays closed after #32400.** `idp_provisioned` now also marks every SCIM-created user (and has always marked a social sign-in), so it no longer means "SSO JIT made it". Steps 2 and 3 carry the boundary: a SCIM-only user has no `sys_account` row at all (the vendor writes none) and fails step 3; a social provider (`google`) is no `sys_sso_provider` row and fails step 3; a SCIM user who later also signed in through SSO owns a subject and fails step 2.

**Why step 2 exists.** The vendor aggregates `active` across every SCIM source of an account, so a second directory linking an account the first one holds could keep a leaver the first one deactivated signed in. Measured today (before this PR): such a create answers `409` on the email. With step 2 removed: an account the first directory still holds is refused by the vendor's profile claim (`409` "Another SCIM source already manages this User profile"), but an account the first directory DELETED is linked (`201`): the delete clears the profile source, so nothing in the vendor's transaction refuses, and the subject is the only guard. Both are pinned.

### `scim-conflict-detail.ts` (new) and `auth-manager-request-routing.ts`

`handleRequest`'s SCIM arm, the one place every `/scim/v2/*` answer leaves, translates a `409` whose SCIM error body carries one of the vendor's four "Better Auth User" details (`dist/index.mjs:6852`, `6909`, `6921`/`6929`, `7018`): "A Better Auth User already uses this email" → "An account with this email already exists" (the card's wording), and "account" for "Better Auth User" in the three others. Only `detail` changes; status, `scimType`, headers and every other answer are passed through as the same object. `auth-manager-after-hook.ts` is not touched.

### `auth-manager-plugin-list.ts`

`identity.resolveUser: createScimSsoAdoptionResolver({ getEngine, readConnection: () => scimRequestScope.getStore() })` beside the existing `reconcileUser`. `auth-manager.ts` is not touched.

## Tests

`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/scim-sso-adoption.test.ts` (new, 17 cases). Every HTTP case goes through `AuthManager.handleRequest()` with a real SCIM bearer, on a real `ObjectQL` over better-sqlite3 with the production identity write guard and break-glass guard registered, so the vendor's transaction, profile claim and uniqueness checks are inside the system under test. Each refusal is the adopt fixture with exactly one fact changed, and asserts the HTTP answer (`409`, `scimType: uniqueness`, the platform wording, no vendor name, no second user, no SCIM link for the connection) and then the judge's reason, so the 409 is that fixture's one cause.

- Adopt: lookup 0 → create `201` linking the existing user (one `sys_user`, one `sys_scim_user` for the connection) → lookup finds the new id → `PATCH active: false` bans the account with the SCIM reason, `source` stays `idp_provisioned`.
- Adopt with the address in another case (`Mixed.Case@ACME.com` against the stored lower-case address).
- `409`, each single-cause: unverified domain; email domain not the provider's; email on a subdomain; not `idp_provisioned`; holds a local password; provider of another organization; provider with no organization while the connection has one; ⛔ bare email with no SSO link; ⛔ bare email linked only to a non-SSO provider; held by another directory; deleted by another directory (the account stays banned).
- A create for an address nobody holds still creates.
- Wording: an email change (`PATCH emails`) onto a held address reads the platform wording (the second vendor site); the translator over all four vendor details keeps status, media type and other headers; any other answer is returned as the same object.

**Red first, on today's behaviour** (judge and translator present, not wired): 13 of 16 red, the adopt cases `409 "A Better Auth User already uses this email"` instead of `201`, every refusal on the vendor wording.

**Ablations** (each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode, anchor 1 → 0, blob changed, restore proven blob == HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty; the suite imports the module from `src`, so no build sits between the mutation and the run):

| # | Defect put back | Red | Observed |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A1 | `domain_verified` filter removed | unverified domain | `201` |
| A2 | email-domain match always true | not the provider's domain; subdomain | `201` ×2 |
| A3 | `source` check removed | not `idp_provisioned` | `201` |
| A4 | local-password check removed | holds a local password | `201` |
| A5 | subject check removed | held by another directory; deleted by another directory | vendor `409` "Another SCIM source already manages this User profile" (wording pin red); `201` |
| A6 | organization filter removed | provider of another organization; provider with no organization | `201` ×2 |
| A7 | ⛔ bare email: an account with no SSO provider link adopted | both bare-email cases | `201` ×2 |
| A8 | translation call removed | 11 refusals + the PATCH wording case | vendor wording |

**Suites and gates, on the final head `cbda0585` (after merging `origin/main` `295d8067`):**

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run`: 264 files, 4874 passed, 10 skipped (taken before the merge, at `be115390`). After the merge (incoming: `packages/metadata` only), `@objectstack/metadata` rebuilt and the four SCIM suites re-run (`scim-sso-adoption`, `scim-deactivation-reconcile-user`, `scim-refusal-audit`, `scim-transaction-scope`): 69/69.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck` (`tsc`, the examples program, `check:test-typecheck`): exit 0.
- `pnpm lint` (repo-wide eslint, `--no-inline-config`): exit 0.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 66 families; each ran with its exit code captured before any pipe: 64 exit 0, 2 exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET, so NOT MEASURED here, CI runs both). `--ran`: 66 derived, 64 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
  - `check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test`: its fixture is pinned to a commit outside this shallow clone. The script is untouched by this diff.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`: reads every package's `dist/`, and 42 packages are unbuilt here. Scoped substitute: `require('@objectstack/plugin-auth')` from its built CJS entry (`dist/index.js`, which carries the new resolver) loads, 183 exports.
- `check-governed-merges --branch HEAD`: 0 of 6 paths governed; 920 changed lines (+916 / -4), under the 3000 threshold.

## Acceptance notes

- **Organization match reading.** The ruling says "an SSO provider of this organization (in V1, this environment)". Read as: the provider's `organization_id` equals the authenticating credential's; both unset (a composition without organizations) counts as one environment-wide boundary; exactly one unset refuses. A provider registered with no active organization (`register-sso-provider.ts` falls back to org-less) beside a credential minted for the Default Organization therefore does not adopt. That is the fail-closed reading; widening it is the seat's or the maintainer's call, not this PR's.
- **Exact domain.** `@better-auth/sso`'s own `domainMatches` accepts a subdomain of a provider domain for its trusted-provider linking; this rule does not (the ruling names the verified domain itself), and that is pinned.
- **Adoption needs D6 on.** `domain_verified` is written only when `OS_SSO_DOMAIN_VERIFICATION` is on and the DNS-TXT check has passed; a deployment without it keeps today's `409`. The cloud docs card (`scim-entra-id.md`, `scim-okta.md`) should say so.
- **`emailVerified` on a case-different address.** On a `manage` link the vendor rewrites the account's email and name from the SCIM profile and sets `emailVerified: false` when the two strings differ (`dist/index.mjs:6926`); a directory sending `Mixed.Case@…` for a stored `mixed.case@…` therefore flips it, as it already does on every SCIM PUT of a SCIM-created user. Noted, not changed.
- **Read-then-write window.** The vendor calls `resolveUser` before its transaction. Steps 1, 3 and 4 are not re-read inside it; step 2 has the vendor's profile claim as an in-transaction backstop for an account another directory still holds. A provider deleted, or a password set, in the milliseconds between is not re-judged.
- No new log line: an adoption leaves the connection-attributed `sys_scim_user` write in the ledger, and a refusal leaves the `scim_refused` row `scim-refusal-audit.ts` already writes (never the `detail`).
- #32115 (SCIM re-activation) is not touched: the only re-activation this PR reaches is the one it refuses (a directory-deleted account is never linked by a second directory).
